A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HUB benchmark. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across table renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of seven unlearning methods, concept-detector validation and qualitative analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations under two further attacks and repeated-seed NSFW results.

M1.justification: HUB's prompt-curation, VLM concept-detection, selective-alignment and pinpoint-ness procedures remain unchanged. The additional attacks extend evaluation; the expanded baseline descriptions do not establish changes to the underlying unlearning algorithms.

E1.justification: The concepts, four categories, five translated languages and existing evaluation datasets are retained. Appendix E.8 adds image-guided prompt attacks through UnlearnDiffAtk and image-conditioned reconstruction through UoC, extending the input conditions beyond v2's Ring-A-Bell prompt attack.

E2.justification: The seven unlearning baselines remain unchanged. The adversarial comparison expands from Ring-A-Bell alone to include UnlearnDiffAtk and UoC, which are actually evaluated alongside it in v3 Tables 30–33 and 36.

E3.justification: Appendix E.8 introduces protocols using 100 optimized prompts for UnlearnDiffAtk and 100 test images with a partial diffusion ratio of 0.1 for UoC. Ring-A-Bell retains 1,000 prompts. Most added Appendix D settings are newly disclosed details, without establishing changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Robustness evaluation expands substantially from one attack to three across all four concept categories. The new tests examine recovery through image-guided prompt optimization and partial image reconstruction, providing evidence beyond the existing CLIP-based prompt attack. Earlier detector validation and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: v2 reports point estimates without systematic uncertainty estimates. New Appendix A.3 reports five different seeds and means with standard deviations for four NSFW metrics across the original model and seven unlearning methods. This introduces substantial uncertainty reporting, although it does not cover every category or metric.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive UnlearnDiffAtk/UoC results and repeated-seed NSFW means. Existing values also change: Table 3's IP multilingual scores move from 0.150 to 0.207 for SLD and 0.057 to 0.031 for MACE, with revised rankings in Table 5. Appendix E.6 corrects the Celebrity/Style assignment of pinpoint-ness values, and SLD's Style PickScore average changes from 21.377 to 21.406. These include reporting corrections and new attack conditions, not demonstrated method improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical content, including baseline objectives and the UCE closed-form solution in Appendix D, is retained. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations appear.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a six-perspective benchmark covering 33 concepts and the finding that no unlearning method excels across all criteria. The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same substantive scope.

C2.justification: Appendix A.3 newly interprets the reported standard deviations below 3% as evidence of statistical stability. The existing explanations of erasure–quality trade-offs, unintended concept removal and limitations of VLM-based evaluation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D now specifies SA epochs and learning rate, ESD variants and training parameters, RECELER steps and learning rate, and MACE budgets and alternative concepts. v3 also adds an explicit project repository link and attack implementation settings. These materially expand reproducibility information, although v2's specific account of two NSFW concept-word sets for MACE is omitted.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for UnlearnDiffAtk, UoC and generative-foundation-model trustworthiness, with discussion distinguishing the attack approaches. The broader positioning relative to existing unlearning methods and benchmarks remains stable.

P1.justification: There are limited prose edits, expanded baseline explanations, new statistical-analysis and attack-evaluation passages, and acknowledgements. Appendix D is renamed 'Baselines and Training Details'; the main narrative and overall appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds uncertainty and multi-attack tables, including summaries that redisplay retained Ring-A-Bell results. It removes v2's aggregate multilingual Table 24 while retaining the five language-specific tables. Tables and surrounding text reflow, but Figures 1–13 retain their visual content and the overall presentation remains similar.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2's single-attack evaluation, v3 provides stronger robustness evidence, including SLD's weakness under UnlearnDiffAtk. Five-seed NSFW estimates, explicit training settings, repository access information and corrected table assignments improve confidence and reproducibility. The gains are limited by partial uncertainty coverage and the omission of v2's specific MACE NSFW word-set description; the central benchmark and conclusions remain stable.
